title: Infosys and Truist Expand Hyderabad AI Capability Centre Past 1,000 Staff
excerpt: Infosys will build, operate and transfer Truist's AI-first Global Capability Center in Hyderabad under an expanded collaboration, consolidating the US bank's India work from multiple suppliers into one model.
body:
• Infosys and Truist will onboard more than 1,000 colleagues this month at Truist's AI-first Global Capability Center in Hyderabad, announced 19 October 2026.
  • Under a build-operate-transfer model, Infosys will build and run the centre before transferring it to Truist as a self-sustaining centre of excellence, with reporting putting the operating period at five years.
  • Truist is consolidating work now handled by multiple suppliers in India into one integrated model covering AI, technology, data and operations.
  • Truist, headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, is a top-10 US commercial bank with total assets of $556 billion as of 30 June 2026.

Infosys has expanded its collaboration with Truist Financial Corporation to build out the US bank's AI-first Global Capability Center in Hyderabad, the companies announced on 19 October 2026 in a joint announcement via PR Newswire. More than 1,000 colleagues will be onboarded at the centre later this month.

The expansion gives Infosys a larger role in how one of America's biggest banks runs technology and operations from India. Truist is consolidating capabilities now delivered through multiple supplier relationships in India into a single, integrated operating model, with Infosys as the partner building and scaling it.

Build, operate, transfer

Infosys will use its Build, Operate and Transfer model to help Truist build, scale and then transition the Hyderabad centre into a self-sustaining centre of excellence. Reporting on the arrangement puts the operating period at five years before full control passes to Truist. The centre will integrate AI, technology, data and operations into one delivery framework, a structure the companies say is designed to reduce third-party dependency, manage global delivery complexity and develop future-ready technology talent.

Infosys will draw on its financial services expertise and its AI offering, Infosys Topaz, to support the build-out. Truist already has contract professionals in India working across engineering, data and operations, and the new model brings that work under a more unified structure.

"Our Global Capability Center in India is a strategic investment in Truist's future. As we accelerate our transformation into a more agile, AI-enabled enterprise, we are intentionally building global capabilities that allow us to move faster, innovate at scale, and better serve our clients."

— Steve Hagerman, Chief Information Officer, Truist

Why Hyderabad, why now

India hosts more than 1,900 global capability centres, according to the companies' announcement, and Hyderabad has become one of the main hubs for US financial services firms building engineering and operations teams. For Truist, headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, the centre is framed as a long-term investment in digital capability rather than a short-term cost programme: the stated goals are better client experiences, faster delivery across geographies and a more digitally enabled, relationship-driven banking model.

Dennis Gada, Infosys executive vice president and global head of banking and financial services, said financial institutions must move from modernising legacy infrastructure to deploying AI at scale across every function, and that Infosys would help Truist build a resilient, scalable digital core with trust and governance built in.

Market reaction and what follows

Infosys shares rose after the announcement, trading at Rs 1,156.20 on 21 October, up 2.26% from the previous session, according to market coverage of the filing. The immediate milestone is the onboarding itself: more than 1,000 colleagues joining the Hyderabad centre this month. The longer test is the transfer — whether the centre reaches the scale and independence the build-operate-transfer model promises, so that Truist ends up owning a working centre of excellence rather than extending a vendor contract.

For Hyderabad's technology workforce, the deal adds another large US banking programme to the city's GCC pipeline, with hiring tied to AI, data and banking operations roles rather than traditional back-office work.
